terms.comment: One skilled in the law, who gave opinions, pleaded and drew up documents (Cic. de Or. 1.212). Also written as two words, jūris cōnsultus.

terms.gloss: advocate: the lawyer who speaks for someone in court
terms.comment: In Cicero’s day a friend called in to stand by a party with advice; from Quintilian on, the pleader himself (Lewis & Short). Traupman’s lawyer for the defence.

terms.gloss: the advocate who pleads a case
evidence: Cic. Rosc. Am. 5: huic causae patrōnus exstitī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Cicero’s word for the speaker who defends a client in court; also a patron or protector.
Often contemptuous: the mere pleader, as against the true orator (Lewis & Short). Traupman’s trial lawyer.

phrases.latin: Sīn autem quaererētur quisnam jūris cōnsultus vērē nōminārētur, eum dīcerem, quī lēgum et cōnsuētūdinis ejus, quā prīvātī in cīvitāte ūterentur, et ad respondendum et ad agendum et ad cavendum perītus esset
phrases.english: But if it were asked who truly deserves the name of lawyer, I would say the man who is skilled in the laws and in the customs that private citizens follow in the state, at giving opinions, at pleading and at drawing up documents

phrases.latin: Jūdicis est semper in causīs vērum sequī, patrōnī nōn numquam vērī simile, etiam sī minus sit vērum, dēfendere
phrases.english: It is always the judge’s part in a trial to follow the truth; the advocate’s, sometimes, to defend what looks like the truth, even if it is less true

sources: Lewis & Short: jurisconsultus · Lewis & Short: advocatus · Lewis & Short: patronus · Lewis & Short: causidicus
